screening_decisions.reason: Review article summarizing packing materials and standards, not an RCT.
Retrospective review study, not an RCT.
Prospective controlled trial comparing revision vs primary ESS, not testing steroid-eluting stents.
RCT but intervention is levobupivacaine-soaked packing (anesthetic), not steroid-eluting stents.
RCT of doxycycline-releasing stents. Doxycycline is an antibiotic/MMP inhibitor, not a corticosteroid. Does not meet intervention criteria.

RCT of steroid-eluting implants, but intervention was in-office placement for recurrent polyposis, not during FESS. Patients were candidates for revision ESS but did not undergo FESS as part of the study intervention.
Epidemiological cross-sectional survey, not an RCT.
Review article on pathogenesis, not an RCT.
RCT involving steroid-eluting spacers (Sinu-Foam). These are classified as packing/dressings rather than sinus stents which provide structural support. Terminology mismatch with 'sinus stents'.
RCT but intervention is lidocaine-soaked packing (anesthetic), not steroid-eluting stents.
RCT but intervention is hyaluronic acid dressing, not steroid-eluting stents.
Guideline/position paper, not an RCT.
RCT but intervention compares glove-coated vs uncoated Merocel packing, not steroid-eluting stents.
Epidemiological prevalence report, not an RCT.

RCT comparing steroid-releasing sinus implants (mometasone furoate) vs non-drug-releasing implants in adult CRS patients undergoing FESS (bilateral ethmoidectomy). Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, steroid-eluting stent intervention, appropriate comparator, adult CRS population, FESS procedure.

RCT involving steroid-impregnated absorbable nasal dressing (Nasopore). This is classified as packing/dressing rather than sinus stents which provide structural support. Terminology mismatch with 'sinus stents'.
RCT but intervention compares glove-coated vs standard PA packing, not steroid-eluting stents.
Prospective review of surgical failures, not an RCT.
Review article on etiology/pathogenesis, not an RCT.

RCT involving steroid-impregnated absorbable nasal dressing (Nasopore). This is classified as packing/dressing rather than sinus stents which provide structural support. Terminology mismatch with 'sinus stents'.

This is an RCT comparing NasoPore (biodegradable synthetic polyurethane foam) with traditional Merocel spacer. Neither intervention is a steroid-eluting stent. The study does not meet the selection criteria as it does not involve steroid-eluting sinus stents.

This is a meta-analysis of 2 prospective randomized trials, not a primary RCT itself. The selection criteria specify inclusion of RCTs, not meta-analyses. While the underlying studies may be relevant, this publication is a secondary analysis.

This RCT evaluates hylan B gel (elastoviscous hylan gel) as a wound dressing for hemostasis. The intervention is not a steroid-eluting stent but rather a gel dressing for bleeding control. Does not meet selection criteria.

This RCT uses triamcinolone-impregnated absorbable gelatin DRESSING, not a steroid-eluting STENT. The selection criteria specifically require steroid-eluting sinus stents. While it involves steroid delivery, the device type (dressing vs stent) does not match the protocol.
This is a retrospective analysis of 970 endoscopic ethmoidectomies, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the study design requirement of the selection criteria.

This is a prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind clinical trial comparing drug-eluting (steroid-eluting) stents with non-drug-eluting stents in CRS patients undergoing FESS. This directly matches the selection criteria: RCT design, steroid-eluting stent intervention, appropriate comparator (non-steroid-eluting stent), correct population (adult CRS patients), and correct setting (after FESS).

This RCT compares hyaluronan resorbable packing (MeroGel) with standard non-resorbable nasal dressing. Neither intervention is a steroid-eluting stent. The study focuses on resorbable vs non-resorbable packing, not steroid-eluting devices.

This appears to be a review/commentary article discussing the correlation between endoscopic/radiological findings and symptoms. It is not a primary RCT and does not meet the study design requirement.

This is described as a 'prospective, multicenter, single-cohort trial' - meaning it is NOT randomized. The selection criteria require RCTs. While it involves steroid-eluting implants, the lack of randomization excludes it from eligibility.

This RCT compares hyaluronic acid nasal packs (Merogel) with no packing. The intervention is not a steroid-eluting stent but rather a hyaluronic acid pack. Does not meet the selection criteria for steroid-eluting stents.
This RCT compares nonabsorbable packing (NAP) with saline irrigation alone. Neither intervention is a steroid-eluting stent. The study does not meet the selection criteria.
This is a postal questionnaire survey assessing CRS prevalence across Europe. It is not an RCT and does not involve any intervention. Does not meet the selection criteria.

This RCT uses triamcinolone-soaked bioabsorbable DRESSING, not a steroid-eluting STENT. The selection criteria specifically require steroid-eluting sinus stents. While it involves steroid delivery via an absorbable material, the device type (dressing/packing vs stent) does not match the protocol requirements.

This RCT compares postoperative systemic prednisone vs placebo, with BOTH groups receiving steroid-eluting spacers. The study does not compare steroid-eluting stents with non-steroid-eluting stents, nasal packing, or no treatment. Instead, it investigates the additive value of systemic steroids when already using steroid-eluting spacers. Does not meet the selection criteria.
This RCT evaluates topical tranexamic acid (TXA) for bleeding control during FESS. The intervention is not a steroid-eluting stent but rather a hemostatic agent. Does not meet the selection criteria.

This is a review article discussing advantages and disadvantages of various stents used in sinus surgery, including drug-releasing stents. It is not a primary RCT and does not meet the study design requirement.

This RCT compares self-cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) hydrogel with carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) viscous foam. Neither intervention is a steroid-eluting stent. The study focuses on wound healing materials, not steroid-eluting devices.
